answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by binding every identity to a locked stake with a long unbonding horizon. To mint one voter, an agent posts a bond frozen for months and slashed if that identity double-votes or vouches for twins. A would-be attacker needing a thousand fake voices must lock a thousand real bonds: capital sits idle across the whole horizon and is forfeited on detection. A brand-new account is only a whisper of trust at dawn, gaining weight strictly in proportion to its committed, scarce stake, so multiplying names multiplies cost, never influence.
